model_blockers: The public RC compiler accepts a serial chain with one fully restrained endpoint, while this specimen is simply supported with two four-point load locations.
The public rectangular RC section has one steel material and lumped top/bottom bar areas; this beam has separate embedded steel and near-surface titanium bars with conductive grout.
The Euler-Bernoulli fiber element has no shear deformation or bond-slip/grout-interface law; the report observes diagonal cracking and late localized debonding.
Concrete tensile law, support compliance, centerline-displacement reference, and CSV sample-time mapping remain unresolved.

post_inspection_predebonding_window.rule: Stop before the first original CSV data row with applied load >= 160 kip; retain original row order and partial unloads.
post_inspection_predebonding_window.rationale: The report attributes abrupt steel/TiAB strain changes to spalling and localized debonding at about 2 kip below the 178 kip ultimate load. The 160 kip ceiling was proposed after source inspection; it is not an independent or blind threshold and does not prove earlier bond or shear effects negligible.
post_inspection_predebonding_window.further_condition: A retrospective development comparison would first need resolved topology, distinct materials, support motion and source-channel semantics with fixed parameters and metrics. Independent blind credit requires a separate response-unseen specimen and prediction lock.
